title: Introduction to Python Programming
baseline: General Python 3.9+ syntax and standard library, checked against the Python 3.13 documentation without relying on newer exclusive features. Web execution replays are generated with CPython 3.14; language coverage and replay runtime are recorded separately.
audience: Readers with no programming experience. Observe the web replays first, then use Section 1.1 to learn how to save files and run programs.
outcomes: Write a runnable program from an empty file
Understand types, branches, loops, and data containers
Organize functions and handle invalid input
Read and write small text, JSON, and CSV files
Write boundary and integration tests for a command-line project
outOfScope: Concurrency, async, generators, and performance tuning

chapters.title: Start programming
chapters.objective: Run scripts, distinguish text from numbers, and perform basic input and output.

chapters.title: Control execution
chapters.objective: Read branches and loops, find boundary errors, and design stopping conditions.

chapters.title: Organize data
chapters.objective: Use shopping lists and price tables to organize data by position, name, or membership.

chapters.title: Organize programs
chapters.objective: Write functions, design interfaces, import modules, and handle expected exceptions.

chapters.title: Build an application
chapters.objective: Handle files, validate formats, test boundaries, and deliver a command-line tool.
